name: Have you taken business objectives into account when making security decisions?
conditionsText:
This applies when:
- Defining security requirements
- Designing security controls
- Making architecture decisions
- Prioritising risks
- Designing operational processes
requirementTitle: Have you taken business objectives into account when making security decisions?
requirementDescription: When choosing security controls, have you considered what the service is trying to achieve for the organisation?
why:
Security should help the organisation achieve its objectives safely, not get in the way.
If security decisions are made without understanding the business purpose, you can end up with:
- Unnecessary controls
- Increased costs
- Delays to delivery
- Reduced business benefits
tasks: Have you taken business objectives into account when making security decisions?

actions.title: Have you taken business objectives into account when making security decisions?
actions.description:
You should be able to show that:
• Business objectives were identified.
• Security requirements were linked to those objectives.
• Security decisions considered business impact.
• Any trade-offs between security and business needs were documented.
